title: Don't believe the hype, stick to the fundamentals
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When something brand new appears, how do you know what it is worth?

groups.heading: How do you value something that has never happened before?

lines.text: I asked the group for a summary of the industrial revolution. A student said: a move from handmaking to machines, processes and new power sources, a rapid evolution of efficiency in manufacturing.

What are the lessons in history, I asked? There were companies whose stock went through the roof because people did not understand how business was going to be revolutionized. They had never seen that kind of growth. I gave the example of a great canal project that raised so much money that it became more profitable to raise money than to build it.

The same thing with the internet, I said. How do you value that? Information is going to flow to every person in the world. A student said: it's hard to value something unpredictable that hasn't happened yet.

groups.heading: Don't believe the hype, stick to the fundamentals

lines.text: Even with real estate, I said, I buy in a destination that has no road, no electricity. People say that's high risk. But I look at population growth and how fast the town is moving, and I see this farmland will be development land in five or six years. You gauge it by the fundamentals.

The problem comes when you are not looking at the fundamentals in a new business and you get blinded by the enormity of something that has never happened before. A famous investor, I said, at the beginning of the internet said he was not even interested, until the dust settled. His message: I have to stick to the fundamentals, because that is what I understand.

I was in this business in the mid-nineties, I said, and luckily I had great mentors. They said: Jose, don't believe the hype. Stick to the fundamentals of a business. Even in the internet, a lot of people said: who cares about profit, it's about market share.
A lot of people grabbed market share and didn't make money, I said, or simply ran out of money.
What are the fundamentals of the thing you are excited about?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the new thing everyone is excited about.
Write its fundamentals: who pays, how much, and what it costs.
Write what you would have to see to believe it is real.
Write who you could ask who lived through a similar boom.
Write the one fundamental you will check this week.

check.q: What did I say my mentors told me in the mid-nineties?
choices: Don't believe the hype, stick to the fundamentals
Grab market share at any cost

check.q: What did a student say is hard to value?
choices: Something unpredictable that hasn't happened yet

check.q: What did I say happens when you get blinded by something new?
choices: You don't stick to the fundamentals

recap: When something new appears, stick to the fundamentals and don't believe the hype.
